findings.title: Dataclass default for `queued` is evaluated once at import, not per instance
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a plain dataclass default, so `timezone.now()` is executed a single time when the module is imported. Every `AssignmentSource` ever constructed (via `from_integration`, `from_dict`, or directly) therefore carries the same process-start timestamp instead of the moment the assignment was queued. Any staleness/TTL/dedup logic that is supposed to read `queued` will be silently wrong. This should be `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` (import `field` from dataclasses). The accompanying test `test_to_dict` only asserts `queued is not None`, so it does not catch this.

findings.title: `from_dict` swallows all parse errors, silently disabling the cycle guard
findings.body: `from_dict` catches `ValueError`/`TypeError` and returns `None`. Callers (`sync_assignee_outbound` at tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py:53-56) then pass `None` into `should_sync`, which treats it as "no source" and proceeds with the outbound sync. If the serialized `assignment_source_dict` is ever malformed or has an unexpected key (e.g., schema drift after the `queued` datetime round-trips), the round-trip silently degrades to no guard at all, re-introducing the very sync loop this PR is meant to fix, with no log or metric to signal it. Consider logging/metrics on failure or making the failure explicit rather than silently returning None.

findings.title: `to_dict` puts a raw datetime into Celery task kwargs
findings.body: `to_dict()` uses `asdict`, which returns `queued` as a `datetime` object, and `sync_group_assignee_outbound` passes this dict straight into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs={...})` (integrations/utils/sync.py:136-144). Celery serializes task kwargs with JSON by default; a raw `datetime` is not JSON-serializable, so `apply_async` can raise at publish time, breaking outbound assignee sync for all integrations. Even under a pickle serializer, `from_dict` rehydrates with `cls(**input_dict)` without any type coercion, so `queued` would be a `str` after a JSON round-trip and the field's type contract is violated. `queued` is not actually used by `should_sync` (only `integration_id` is compared), so it should either be excluded from the serialized payload or explicitly (de)serialized.

findings.title: No test that other integrations still receive the outbound update
findings.body: The PR's stated behavior is that only the originating integration is suppressed while "other integrations still propagate changes outward." The new `test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration` only asserts the negative case (`mock_sync_assignee_outbound.assert_not_called()` for the source integration). There is no test with two linked integrations verifying that the non-source integration's outbound sync is still invoked, so a regression where the new `sync_source` guard over-suppresses (e.g., comparing wrong id) would go undetected.
